  SAVE THE LAMPASAS RESPONSE TO ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY,
  LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION’S OBJECTIONS TO,
            AND MOTION TO STRIKE, INTERVENOR TESTIMONY

         Save the Lampasas files this Response to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (Oncor)

  and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation’s (LCRA) (collectively, the Applicants)

  Objections to, and Motions to Strike, Intervenor Testimony (AIS Item No. 4726), and would

  respectfully show as follows:


                                        I.       RESPONSE
         Applicants argue that certain statements of direct testimonies of Suzanne Thompson and

  Rayma Chase should be stricken from the record on the grounds that the specific statements are

  “Hearsay; Non-Expert Opinion.”1 For reference, both Suzanne Thompson and Rayma Chase

  include the following statement:

         We are particularly concerned about the potential long-term health effects of
         chronic exposure to the extremely low-frequency (ELF) electromagnetic fields
         generated by a 765-kV transmission line. The International Agency for Research
         on Cancer (IARC), an agency of the World Health Organization, classifies ELF

  1
    Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation's Objections to, and
  Motion to Strike, Intervenor Testimony (May 18, 2026) (Objections).
                                                                                                     Page 2 of 3


          magnetic fields as “possibly carcinogenic to humans” (Group 2B).
          Epidemiological studies have reported an association between residential
          exposure to magnetic fields from high-voltage power lines and an approximately
          doubled risk of childhood leukemia.2


          Contrary to the Applicants’ generalized objections, this statement is not hearsay nor are

Rayma and Suzanne purporting to be providing an expert opinion. Under the Texas Rules of

Evidence (TRE), hearsay is a statement that “a party offers in evidence to prove the truth of the

matter asserted in the statement.”3 The first sentence of the testimony is offered to express

personal opinions and concerns of the affected property owners. The second and third sentences

are not offered for their truth, but rather to demonstrate why Rayma and Suzanne are having

feelings of concern about their health by being in proximity to a transmission line. Further, it

does not purport to be expert testimony, and as a result, it is admissible as lay opinion under TRE

701. Therefore, neither of the Applicants objections should be sustained.


                                            II.       PRAYER
          For the foregoing reasons, Save the Lampasas respectfully request that the Administrative

Law Judges enter an Order: (i) overruling all Applicant objections to the testimony of Suzanne

Thompson and Rayma Chase (AIS Item No. 4726); (ii) admitting the testimony of Suzanne

Thompson and Rayma Chase, with all exhibits (AIS Items Nos. 4497 and 4482, respectfully),

with such weight as the Administrative Law Judges deem appropriate after consideration of the

full record; and (iii) granting any and all further relief to which Save the Lampasas may be justly

entitled.

owner of Dillingham Family Ranch, and Save the Lampasas at bates 07 (AIS No. 4482) (May 13, 2026).
